subsystems.name: Transcranial ultrasound array
subsystems.role: delivers focused acoustic energy through the skull into a small brain volume.

subsystems.name: Image guidance and planning
subsystems.role: targets the treatment volume and corrects for skull distortion.
parts: skull segmentation and acoustic simulation software

subsystems.name: Microbubble agent
subsystems.role: circulates in blood vessels and oscillates under ultrasound to open the barrier.

subsystems.name: Cavitation monitoring and control
subsystems.role: detects bubble activity and adjusts power to keep opening safe and reversible.

subsystems.name: Safety and verification workflow
subsystems.role: confirms that the barrier opened where intended and resealed afterwards.

buildSteps.title: Design the array for the skull
buildSteps.detail: Element layout, frequency and aperture are chosen to penetrate bone while keeping the focus small enough for millimetre-scale targets.

buildSteps.title: Plan the treatment from imaging
buildSteps.detail: MRI or CT scans are segmented; software models skull thickness and density, then simulates and adjusts the acoustic field for each target.

buildSteps.title: Build and assemble the transducer
buildSteps.detail: Piezoelectric elements are diced, wired, bonded to matching layers and mounted in a water-filled helmet that couples sound into the head.

buildSteps.title: Integrate imaging and control
buildSteps.detail: The array is registered to the scanner or navigation system, and passive detectors are calibrated to listen for microbubble emissions.

buildSteps.title: Prepare and administer microbubbles
buildSteps.detail: A clinically approved lipid-shelled contrast agent is prepared and infused intravenously while the patient is positioned in the device.

buildSteps.title: Sonicate with feedback
buildSteps.detail: Power is ramped slowly; bubble emissions are monitored and the system adjusts output to sustain gentle opening without excessive cavitation.

buildSteps.title: Verify opening and resealing
buildSteps.detail: Contrast-enhanced MRI shows where the barrier is permeable; repeat imaging hours later confirms it has closed.

buildSteps.title: Follow the clinical protocol
buildSteps.detail: Neurological checks and imaging are repeated after treatment, and the procedure is repeated only within trial safety limits.

prerequisites.why: phased arrays and skull-correction software can already steer and focus sound through the intact skull.
clinically approved agents provide the oscillating bubbles that mechanically open tight junctions.
targeting and skull modelling depend on high-resolution imaging and acoustic simulation.
passive detectors work in trials, but robust closed-loop control across patients is still being refined.
early trials show reversible opening, but long-term safety and repeat dosing are not yet established.

pathway.milestone: early-phase trials opening the barrier in glioblastoma, Alzheimer's disease and other brain conditions
pathway.unlocks: proof that the procedure is feasible and reversible in patients.

pathway.milestone: trials combining opening with delivered drugs, antibodies or gene vectors
pathway.unlocks: evidence that better brain penetration improves outcomes.

pathway.milestone: larger trials with standardised dosing and safety monitoring
pathway.unlocks: the data needed for regulatory approval in a first indication.

pathway.milestone: routine clinical use, possibly with non-MRI guidance and multi-target treatment
pathway.unlocks: repeatable, outpatient delivery of large molecules to the brain.
